findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py:899–936 checks pure head movement and a reflog entry anywhere between delegation opening and recovery, but never checks that the incident predates receipts or rejects self-attributed receipts. A delegated child can run project_sync.py from its assigned worktree, advancing integration main and producing a receipt naming itself. Normal recording correctly refuses this; recover-external-advance then accepts the resulting friction event and reflog, replaces the baseline head, and allows recording. No forged evidence is needed. The friction timestamp proves the child returned before the event, but does not establish who performed the earlier advance.
findings.summary: Claude recovery can legalize a current, self-attributed containment violation rather than only a historical false positive.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/project_sync.py:20–41 accepts --remote, validates and fetches that selected remote, and fast-forwards successfully. Its new receipt call at lines 42–48 invokes template/scripts/delegation_containment.py:378, which unconditionally resolves refs/remotes/origin/<main>. With only an upstream remote, project_sync.py --remote upstream therefore raises after the merge and writes no receipt. Previously this supported invocation completed successfully; retrying now takes the equal-state return and never repairs the missing receipt.
findings.summary: Synchronizing from a supported non-origin remote now fails after changing integration HEAD when origin/main is absent.
